purpose: Freeze, append-only, the HPO correction to CHECKPOINT B0's B0-11-zero-production-data postcondition: 'zero production data' means no tenant/user/transactional/application-production data, NOT literally zero rows in every table. An explicitly governed baseline catalog seed is permitted ONLY when the baseline manifest classifies its migration dml as 'global-catalog', bound one-to-one to a deterministic seed specification. This is a narrow, closed-world exception — not a DML allowlist, not a table-name bypass, not an inferred future exemption. It resolves the sole remaining CHECKPOINT B0 red (17/18) found by the first complete 64-unit isolated-cluster rehearsal under HPO-ODS-W2-03, and does not reopen that provisioning repair, migration 0040, the B1 migrations, or the B1 evidence semantic audit.

HPO-ODS-W2-04.title: GOVERN_BASELINE_GLOBAL_CATALOG_SEED_SEMANTICS
HPO-ODS-W2-04.b0_11_semantics_before: requirement: 'Every probed table holds zero rows.' — literally zero, no exception, and its own detail message ('0018 is the baseline's only DML') was already stale against the manifest's own dml classification of 0040 as global-catalog (added 2026-08-31, predating this rehearsal).
HPO-ODS-W2-04.b0_11_semantics_after: requirement: every table the baseline creates holds ZERO rows, EXCEPT a table named by an explicitly governed global-catalog seed specification, which must hold EXACTLY its declared row count — no more, no fewer. The exception is closed-world and bijective: every manifest unit classified dml='global-catalog' must have exactly one seed specification, and every seed specification's declared unit must exist and still be classified dml='global-catalog', with its declared migration hash matching the manifest's own live-verified pin. A drift in either direction (an unregistered global-catalog unit, an orphaned seed spec, or a hash mismatch) is a FAILED postcondition, not a silent pass.

exports: GlobalCatalogSeedSpec interface: { unitId, file, table, expectedMigrationSha256, expectedRowCount }
GLOBAL_CATALOG_SEED_SPECS: readonly GlobalCatalogSeedSpec[] — exactly one entry, for 0040/public.governed_model_registry/8, pinned independently to the migration's own LF-normalized SHA-256

validateGlobalCatalogClosedWorld(units, specs): the bijection + hash-drift check, called BOTH by a dedicated static test and by B0-11 itself at evaluation time (defense in depth — the manifest classification is consulted live, never assumed)
expectedRowCountsFromClosedWorld(tables, specs): builds the per-table expected-row-count map B0-11 compares against (0 for every table not named by a spec)
architecture.single_source_of_classification: db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts BASELINE_UNITS[*].dml remains the ONLY place a unit is classified global-catalog. global-catalog-seeds.ts never re-classifies; it only supplies the row-count/table identity a classified unit's DML doesn't otherwise carry, and refuses if the manifest disagrees with what it expects.
architecture.b0_11_change: db/hosted/baseline-postconditions.ts: the B0-11 check first calls validateGlobalCatalogClosedWorld against the live BASELINE_UNITS; on failure it fails B0-11 naming the exact contract violation. It then compares every observed row count against the closed-world expectation (0 by default, spec.expectedRowCount for a spec's table) instead of against a flat zero, and fails on ANY mismatch in either direction.

not_authorized: a generic DML allowlist keyed by table name alone
a hardcoded row-count check disconnected from migration/hash identity
an exception inferred for any future migration not carrying dml='global-catalog' with a matching seed spec
any relaxation of B0-11 for organizations, projects, users, evidence, calculations, interactions, or any other tenant-scoped table

protected_grant_rationale: All implementation surfaces (db/hosted/global-catalog-seeds.ts, db/hosted/baseline-postconditions.ts, tests/hosted/**, scripts/baseline-rehearsal-local.ts, artifacts/baseline-rehearsal/latest.json) fall outside every DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERN in scripts/ods-scope.ts. No HPO-ODS-W2-04 grant is registered; ordinary --allow governs this change.

positive.P2: every other baseline table at 0 rows — B0-11 PASS
positive.P3: closed-world bijection: 1 manifest global-catalog unit <-> 1 seed spec, both directions

negative.N3: any unrelated governed-zero table (e.g. public.organizations) holds 1 row — B0-11 FAIL
negative.N4: a hypothetical manifest unit classified global-catalog with no seed spec — validateGlobalCatalogClosedWorld FAIL
negative.N5: a seed spec whose declared unit is not classified global-catalog (or does not exist) — validateGlobalCatalogClosedWorld FAIL
negative.N6: a seed spec's pinned migration hash disagreeing with the manifest's live unit hash — validateGlobalCatalogClosedWorld FAIL

mutation.M1: revert B0-11 to flat zero-row semantics — the current legitimate 8-row catalog state must then fail, proving the old check was actually enforcing something and the new one is a deliberate, narrow relaxation
mutation.M2: replace the exact governed-seed comparison with a bare 'this table may contain rows' allowance — N1 (the extra-row control) must still catch it
mutation.M3: hardcode the expected row count with no hash binding — N6 (hash-drift control) must still catch a migration edit
